subject: Marketplace billing onboarding and SLA exemptions for CloudFolio pilot
messages:
From: Elena Morozova <elena@cloudfolio.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudFolio Billing <billing@cloudfolio.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace billing onboarding and SLA exemptions for pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudFolio is excited to pilot Redwood’s inference platform behind a private offer. Before we spin up the pilot, our finance and procurement teams need two quick confirmations: 

1) Billing flow: can Redwood route private-offer billing via a monthly invoice to billing@cloudfolio.com instead of through marketplace metered charges? If not, what mapping would you recommend for metered-hour SKUs so our internal accounting maps correctly?

2) SLA / credits: our legal team is asking whether we can accept an initial 90-day SLA exception (no service credits for the pilot) while we verify integration stability, with SLA terms reverting to the standard marketplace SLOs after the pilot. Is that something Redwood will support for early-stage pilots?

Attached is a first-pass PO and the expected pilot usage profile. Happy to hop on a quick call with your billing ops if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morozova
Head of Cloud Partnerships, CloudFolio
elena@cloudfolio.com
+1 415-555-0291

Attachments: CloudFolio_PO.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@cloudfolio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace billing onboarding and SLA exemptions for pilot

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the PO. Welcome aboard. Quick response while I loop in billing/partner ops.

Short answers:
- We can accommodate invoicing to billing@cloudfolio.com via our private-offer billing flow, but there are two configuration items we need to confirm: SKU mapping for metered hours (we prefer a 1:1 hourly SKU -> customer consumption mapping for accurate cost allocation) and whether CloudFolio prefers consolidated monthly invoice or per-usage line items.
- SLA exception: we can approve a 90-day pilot exemption on a case-by-case basis. We typically require a documented mutual action plan and a sign-off from Partner Ops + Legal. For operational transparency we ask that any SLA exceptions include an agreed monitoring runbook and escalation contacts.

Attached: marketplace_sku_map.xlsx (template) and a DocuSign draft for the mutual action plan (pilot_mop_docusign.pdf). Can you confirm expected monthly commit (or typical peak hourly) so we can suggest SKU bundling and invoice thresholds?

Proposed next steps:
1) CloudFolio confirms commit estimate and whether you want a consolidated invoice or line-item metered invoice.
2) Ben from Partner Ops and Karthik from Billing will review and propose the exact invoice routing and tax handling.
3) Sign DocuSign mutual action plan and we’ll stand up the private-offer entitlement.

I’ll schedule a 30 min billing ops walk-through for tomorrow if that works for your team.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships (North America)
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 617-555-0112

Attachments: marketplace_sku_map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), pilot_mop_docusign.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@cloudfolio.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace billing onboarding and SLA exemptions for pilot

Elena — looping in Partner Ops & Billing. A few clarifying items from our side to make sure the mapping is correct:

- Invoice shape: we can do consolidated monthly invoices with per-SKU line items, or push through marketplace metered charges. For accounting simplicity we often recommend consolidated monthly with the hourly SKU listed as usage lines; please let us know if your AP needs a single net amount vs line-level detail.
- SKU bundling: please fill the attached SKU map with expected average hourly usage and any committed minimums. That allows us to propose whether to create a small reserved capacity SKU vs pure on-demand metered SKU.
- Tax & PO: if CloudFolio requires our tax form/TIN to appear on the invoice, send over your vendor onboarding form and we’ll populate the vendor fields. Also confirm remit-to address for wire vs ACH.

One operational ask: if we do the 90-day SLA exemption, we need CloudFolio to accept our pilot-runbook items: (1) enable logging to our shared S3 bucket for the pilot; (2) engage tier-2 support on the first escalation; (3) schedule a weekly health sync during the pilot. This keeps both sides aligned in case of incidents.

Drive link for internal billing notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/drive/marketplace/billing-mapping-DF-2029-0471

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Partner Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Elena Morozova <elena@cloudfolio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudFolio Billing <billing@cloudfolio.com>, CloudFolio Sales <sales@cloudfolio.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace billing onboarding and SLA exemptions for pilot

On Thu, May 23, 2029 at 12:18 PM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — looping in Partner Ops & Billing. A few clarifying items from our side to make sure the mapping is correct:
> 
> - Invoice shape: we can do consolidated monthly invoices with per-SKU line items, or push through marketplace metered charges. For accounting simplicity we often recommend consolidated monthly with the hourly SKU listed as usage lines; please let us know if your AP needs a single net amount vs line-level detail.

Thanks, Monica — consolidated monthly with line-level detail is ideal for our AP so we can reconcile against internal chargeback. We will not accept a single net amount.

> - SKU bundling: please fill the attached SKU map with expected average hourly usage and any committed minimums. That allows us to propose whether to create a small reserved capacity SKU vs pure on-demand metered SKU.

Attached: CloudFolio_PO.pdf (application/pdf) — the PO includes target ranges. For an initial pilot (90 days) we expect ~12,000 GPU-hours total (roughly 135 GPU-hours/day peak). We can update if initial telemetry diverges.

> - Tax & PO: if CloudFolio requires our tax form/TIN to appear on the invoice, send over your vendor onboarding form and we’ll populate the vendor fields. Also confirm remit-to address for wire vs ACH.

We’ll fill your vendor form and send the remit-to info to billing@cloudfolio.com. Also: do you need CloudFolio’s tax ID on Redwood’s invoice or on the marketplace record?

> One operational ask: if we do the 90-day SLA exemption, we need CloudFolio to accept our pilot-runbook items: (1) enable logging to our shared S3 bucket for the pilot; (2) engage tier-2 support on the first escalation; (3) schedule a weekly health sync during the pilot. This keeps both sides aligned in case of incidents.

Understood and agreed. We can enable S3 logging and commit a named tier-2 contact. Weekly health sync OK.

Next: I’ll have our AP attend the billing walk-through tomorrow. Please send calendar invite.

—
Elena
Head of Cloud Partnerships, CloudFolio
